source_text.body:
Call doctors' offices and book the earliest in-network appointment
An AI agent phones offices for the user to find the earliest in-network slot and book specialists, dentists, follow-ups, or new primary care visits.
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The post says the team at August built an AI agent that calls doctors’ offices on a user’s behalf to find the earliest in-network appointment and book it, covering specialists, dentists, follow-ups, and new primary care visits in the US. Users join a waitlist and describe the appointment they need through the form or by DM, and the company says the agent then takes over the calling and booking work.
How it went
The source reports that over the previous few weeks the agent spent 24,286 minutes on hold for early users, including 366 minutes for one person. The thread does not give booking success rates, turnaround times, or examples of failed cases.
Worth knowing
It was offered as a free US beta through a waitlist, and the post asks people not to share health details publicly in comments.
Try it yourself
with
Manus
Copy prompt
Find the earliest in-network appointment for [type: specialist, dentist, follow-up, or new primary care] near [my city/zip] with my insurance [plan name]. Check each practice's availability online and call them if I've enabled phone calls, then list the top [3] options with date, time, address, and phone number. Before booking or sharing my date of birth, member ID, or any personal details, pause and show me what you're about to send. You're done when I've approved one option and you've confirmed the booking.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/betatests/comments/1y1drp1/got_a_doctors_appointment_you_keep_putting_off
